title: Cab's 'Play it, Foots!' and earlier work with Luis Russell
summary: Cab's shouts made Thomas famous; he recalls playing earlier with Luis Russell's New Orleans players, which fed his ad-lib style.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And then we started this thing on the air... And Cab really made me famous. It wasn't me. I played them solos, and he'd say, "Play it, Foots!" and I'd be playing the best I could. And I'd just keep playing all that stuff I knew, because playing with Jelly... See, if you play with New Orleans guys, that stuff gets in your head. Because I'd also played with Luis Russell, you know.
Yeah. Because I think he picked it up... Because Luis Russell was from New Orleans, you know.
Did you get to play with Zutty?

Yes. And Higgenbotham... He was a heck of a trombone player. And Cootie Williams. I told Cootie one time, I said, 'Cootie...' He didn't remember. I know Cootie was with Luis Russell, because he was there at the same time I was. Because he came in there... That was the first band he played with in New York! Luis Russell was a good piano player and he had a job on Lenox Avenue at one of them clubs. I played with him first.

And by the time I got to the Missourians, I was a pretty good musicians by that time, because I'd gone through it with Jelly Roll, and come back to New York... But I'd been ad-libbing all my life, from the days out at school. And when I went to Minot, playing with a little small band, ain't nobody in the band to play solos but you -- and the piano player. Because the guitar didn't do nothin' but strum; he didn't do no pickin'. So I just had that talent to play. And I liked the New Orleans style of playing, because it...
